chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ahmad ibn A'izh, from Al-Husayn ibn Mukhtar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Does a man enter into Ihram in black cloth?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He enters into Ihram in black cloth, and the deceased is shrouded in it.'

key_terms.يُحْرِمُ: Enters into the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to wear black clothes during Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies that black garments are permissible for the pilgrim in Ihram, countering potential concerns about color restrictions, and extends this permissibility to the shrouding of the deceased. It reflects the Shia scholarly view that the prohibition in Ihram primarily targets specific mixed fabrics or distinct colors like yellow, while black remains a neutral and acceptable choice for both ritual states and burial.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Ahmad bin Aiz, from Al Husayn Bin Mukhtar who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘Can the man Ihraam himself in black cloth?’ Heasws said: ‘He cannot be Ihraamed in black clothes, nor can the deceased be shrouded in it’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ahmad has narrated from ibn Mahbub from al-‘Ala’ ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“I once asked one of the two Imam, (abu Ja’far or abu ‘Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, about a man who assumes the state of Ihram in dirty cloths. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, I do not say it is unlawful but I like it to be cleansed and its cleansing is washing. One does not wash his cloths of Ihram before coming out of the state of Ihram, even if it becomes dirty, unless it is because of sexual activities (because of which Ghusl (bath) is obligatory) or something of such nature; then one washes them clean . ‘“
